milestones.title: Year 1 Q1 — Contracts and safe foundation (Aug–Oct 2026)
milestones.description: A contributor can install CARTOGRAPH, inspect the graph/evidence contract, and run a deterministic fixture scan. Exit gate: schema, provenance, privacy, and resource ceilings are tested; clean-install CI passes.

milestones.title: Year 1 Q2 — TypeScript/Express extraction (Nov 2026–Jan 2027)
milestones.description: Bounded TypeScript and Express repositories produce useful graphs with honest unsupported diagnostics. Exit gate: at least five curated fixtures, construct-family precision/recall, and no silent dynamic edges.

milestones.title: Year 1 Q3 — Reviewable revisions (Feb–Apr 2027)
milestones.description: A maintainer can compare two revisions and inspect a self-contained report. Exit gate: versioned JSON diff, golden mutation tests, offline HTML, stable CLI behavior, and a baseline benchmark.

milestones.title: Year 1 Q4 — CI and v0.1 adoption (May–Jul 2027)
milestones.description: A repository can run CARTOGRAPH in a read-only GitHub Action and install a reproducible OSS release. Exit gate: fork-safe Action, three representative reports, package smoke test, and security review.

milestones.title: Year 2 Q1 — Refactor-stable identity (Aug–Oct 2027)
milestones.description: Ordinary moves, renames, and supported refactors do not appear as unrelated architecture objects. Exit gate: identity rules, ambiguity behavior, migration tooling, and rename/move fixtures are public.

milestones.title: Year 2 Q2 — Change-control policies (Nov 2027–Jan 2028)
milestones.description: Teams can express bounded graph constraints with informational or enforcing CI behavior. Exit gate: versioned local policy schema, evidence-linked violations, stable exit modes, and measured false-positive fixtures.

milestones.title: Year 2 Q3 — ADR traceability (Feb–Apr 2028)
milestones.description: Local architecture decisions can be linked to graph objects and reviewed beside changed evidence. Exit gate: stale/missing references are detected and reports remain useful offline.

milestones.title: Year 2 Q4 — Extension contract (May–Jul 2028)
milestones.description: External contributors can implement an adapter without changing the core. Exit gate: adapter API, capability manifest, conformance kit, and support matrix are public.

milestones.title: Year 3 Q1 — Language expansion gate (Aug–Oct 2028)
milestones.description: CARTOGRAPH validates one bounded non-TypeScript adapter or records why expansion should be deferred. Exit gate: language-neutral mapping, conformance evidence, and unsupported coverage are published.

milestones.title: Year 3 Q2 — Runtime reconciliation experiment (Nov 2028–Jan 2029)
milestones.description: Users can optionally reconcile local OpenTelemetry observations with static edges without a hosted collector. Exit gate: versioned local input, deterministic classifications, synthetic evaluation, redaction, and explicit opt-in.

milestones.title: Year 3 Q3 — OSS hardening and community scale (Feb–Apr 2029)
milestones.description: Larger repositories and new contributors receive predictable performance, security, upgrade, and support behavior. Exit gate: budgets, bounded fuzz/property tests, compatibility policy, and adopter feedback.

milestones.title: Year 3 Q4 — Traction-based strategy gate (May–Jul 2029)
milestones.description: The project chooses its next investment from evidence instead of assuming a hosted product is warranted. Exit gate: public OSS scorecard and a privacy/security-gated strategy ADR.

milestones.title: Year 4 Q1 — Bounded queries and workspace scale (Aug–Oct 2029)
milestones.description: Reviewers can run evidence-backed impact queries on bounded large graphs and package workspaces. Exit gate: deterministic query semantics, resource ceilings, large-graph benchmarks, workspace coverage, and reviewer-utility evidence pass.

milestones.title: Year 4 Q2 — Offline multi-repository composition (Nov 2029–Jan 2030)
milestones.description: Teams can compose independently produced snapshots and bounded external indexes without uploading source. Exit gate: namespace, boundary, provenance, privacy, resource, and representative portfolio evaluations pass.

milestones.title: Year 4 Q3 — Governed review and interoperability (Feb–Apr 2030)
milestones.description: Reviewers can resolve owners, inspect findings, verify scoped waivers, and use accessible portable review surfaces. Exit gate: lifecycle integrity, fork safety, accessibility, interoperability, authorization-boundary fixtures, and maintainer-load evaluation pass.

milestones.title: Year 4 Q4 — Reproducible assurance bundles (May–Jul 2030)
milestones.description: Maintainers can export bounded architecture evidence without making compliance claims. Exit gate: canonical bundles, provenance, signing, SBOM linkage, local redaction, cache correctness, and independent offline replay pass.

milestones.title: Year 5 Q1 — Longitudinal architecture intelligence (Aug–Oct 2030)
milestones.description: Maintainers can study architecture evolution locally without hidden telemetry or predictive claims. Exit gate: versioned history, provenance, gaps, retention, debt indicators, scale, validity, and safe local export boundaries pass.

milestones.title: Year 5 Q2 — Governed remediation and policy portability (Nov 2030–Jan 2031)
milestones.description: CARTOGRAPH can propose bounded remediation while policies remain portable and humans retain control. Exit gate: suggestion separation, isolated preview, allowlisted validation, approval, privacy, policy compatibility, revocation, and red-team gates pass.

milestones.title: Year 5 Q3 — Ecosystem and research validation (Feb–Apr 2031)
milestones.description: Core claims are tested against portable formats, public corpora, representative repositories, and independent reviewers. Exit gate: reproducible methods, comparative evidence, negative results, limitations, and explicit expansion decisions are published.

milestones.title: Year 5 Q4 — LTS sustainability and strategy renewal (May–Jul 2031)
milestones.description: The project enters its next cycle with a support model, succession plan, and terminal investment decision. Exit gate: reproducible LTS release, migration and recovery rehearsal, security audit, retrospective, and continue, scale, transfer, maintain, or sunset ADR pass.

issues.title: Publish product charter, support matrix, and non-goals
issues.problemOutcome: Scope ambiguity would cause premature framework expansion and misleading claims.
acceptanceCriteria: Public charter identifies users, supported constructs, unknown semantics, versioning, success metrics, and explicit non-goals.
Support matrix has an owner and a documented review process.

issues.title: Complete threat model and privacy data-flow review
issues.problemOutcome: Source parsing, static reports, and fork pull requests create avoidable data and execution risk.
acceptanceCriteria: Threat model covers CLI, parser inputs, report generation, GitHub tokens, fork pull requests, dependencies, path leakage, and optional traces.
Mitigations and security tests are mapped, and default network-offline behavior is verified.

issues.title: Establish installable TypeScript CLI/package skeleton
issues.problemOutcome: Contributors need a reproducible executable baseline.
acceptanceCriteria: A clean checkout supports npm ci, tests, package creation, cartograph --help, and cartograph --version.
Supported LTS policy and stable top-level exit behavior are documented, and a no-op scan does not execute repository code.

issues.title: Define and validate GraphSnapshot schema v0.1
issues.problemOutcome: Extractors and downstream tools need a shared, versioned contract.
acceptanceCriteria: JSON Schema defines revision metadata, nodes, edges, evidence references, diagnostics, and schema version.
A validator rejects malformed snapshots, and representative fixtures are checked in.

issues.title: Enforce evidence and provenance invariants
issues.problemOutcome: Architecture output is not trustworthy when edges cannot be traced to source evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Every emitted edge has evidence references or an explicit unresolved reason.
Evidence includes normalized path, span, extractor/version, confidence, and content hash; raw snippets are absent by default; invariant and redaction tests pass.

issues.title: Add public OSS contribution and security baseline
issues.problemOutcome: Contributors and reporters need predictable project norms.
acceptanceCriteria: README, CONTRIBUTING, Code of Conduct, SECURITY policy, issue templates, support policy, and required CI checks are present.
Disclosure and dependency-update ownership are documented.

issues.title: Freeze schema compatibility and versioning policy
issues.problemOutcome: Consumers cannot safely automate upgrades while graph, evidence, and diagnostic contracts change implicitly.
acceptanceCriteria: A compatibility policy defines additive, breaking, deprecated, and migration-required changes for snapshots, reports, policies, and adapters.
CI rejects an unreviewed schema-version change and a fixture proves old-version read behavior or an actionable migration error.

issues.title: Add a versioned machine-readable configuration contract
issues.problemOutcome: Ad hoc configuration makes scans hard to reproduce and review safely in CI.
acceptanceCriteria: A JSON Schema validates include/exclude rules, resource ceilings, extractor selection, output mode, and policy references.
Configuration defaults are deterministic, unknown fields fail or warn according to a documented mode, and path values cannot escape the repository root.

issues.title: Build safe TypeScript program loader
issues.problemOutcome: Scans need deterministic project discovery without executing project code.
acceptanceCriteria: Loader handles documented tsconfig variants, project references, path aliases, and exclusions.
Dependency/build directories are excluded; tests prove no build scripts or arbitrary modules execute; file order is deterministic.
Default pre-v0.1 ceilings are 20,000 selected source files, 2 MiB per file, 64 MiB total selected source bytes, and 30 seconds wall-clock analysis; exceeding a ceiling fails closed with a diagnostic.

issues.title: Extract TypeScript module/import/export edges
issues.problemOutcome: Module structure is the first useful architecture signal for TypeScript repositories.
acceptanceCriteria: Supported import, export, re-export, and documented dynamic-import cases produce typed edges with source evidence.
Unsupported cases produce diagnostics, and golden snapshots are deterministic.

issues.title: Extract bounded Express route, router, and middleware edges
issues.problemOutcome: Express architecture is often implicit in route registration and middleware chains.
acceptanceCriteria: A documented subset of direct route, router, and middleware declarations is extracted.
Route and middleware evidence points to source spans; dynamic registration is reported as unknown; fixture outputs match expected edge sets.

issues.title: Add explicit unsupported-construct diagnostics
issues.problemOutcome: Dynamic JavaScript patterns can produce false confidence if silently ignored or guessed.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned diagnostic registry assigns every supported unknown case a unique code, severity, evidence location, and actionable remediation; golden fixtures lock the public output.
Unsupported or dynamic constructs never silently emit confident edges; diagnostics appear in snapshots and later reports with actionable guidance.

issues.title: Build extractor fixture corpus and evaluator
issues.problemOutcome: Architecture extraction needs measurable regression evidence rather than subjective screenshots.
acceptanceCriteria: At least five curated fixtures cover simple modules, project references, routers, middleware, and dynamic or unsupported cases.
Expected edge sets are versioned; evaluator reports precision and recall by construct family; CI catches unexpected changes.

issues.title: Implement canonical snapshot validation and serialization
issues.problemOutcome: Non-deterministic ordering makes diffs noisy and undermines trust.
acceptanceCriteria: Nodes, edges, diagnostics, paths, and metadata use canonical ordering and normalization.
Repeated runs produce byte-identical snapshots; invalid snapshots fail with actionable errors; normalized cross-platform fixtures agree.

issues.title: Define the capability and unknown-semantics registry
issues.problemOutcome: Users need to distinguish unsupported constructs from confidently empty architecture results.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned registry maps extractor capabilities to diagnostic codes, confidence levels, and documented examples.
Snapshots and reports expose the registry version and never upgrade an unknown construct to a confident edge without evidence.

issues.title: Establish fixture licensing and provenance manifests
issues.problemOutcome: A growing corpus can become legally ambiguous or impossible to reproduce.
acceptanceCriteria: Every checked-in repository fixture has a source, license, commit/reference, transformation note, and local redistribution decision.
A validator fails when a fixture is missing provenance or includes generated output without a declared reason.

issues.title: Enforce deterministic resource and cancellation policy
issues.problemOutcome: Unbounded repositories can exhaust developer or CI resources before producing useful evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: File-count, byte, archive, memory, wall-clock, and report-cardinality ceilings are configurable and fail closed with stable diagnostics.
Cancellation cleans temporary materialization and never emits a partial snapshot as a successful result.

issues.title: Resolve inherited tsconfig and solution-reference graphs
issues.problemOutcome: Multi-package TypeScript repositories produce incomplete graphs when compiler configuration is inherited or layered.
acceptanceCriteria: The loader resolves extends chains, solution references, per-project roots, and inherited path/exclusion settings without executing config code.
Fixtures cover cycles, missing bases, mixed composite projects, and deterministic diagnostics for unsupported configuration.

issues.title: Model package exports, import maps, and NodeNext resolution
issues.problemOutcome: Modern package boundaries are misrepresented when exports/imports maps and module modes are ignored.
acceptanceCriteria: Supported package.json exports/imports conditions and NodeNext/Node16 resolution outcomes become evidence-backed module edges.
Ambiguous or environment-dependent condition branches emit explicit diagnostics with the selected condition set.

issues.title: Add revision and base/head orchestration
issues.problemOutcome: Users need to compare commits without requiring a service.
acceptanceCriteria: CLI accepts a working tree, two local Git refs, or two snapshot paths.
Implicit remote access is absent; dirty-tree behavior is documented; fixture tests cover base/head resolution failures.
Archive and materialization are bounded to 128 MiB archive output, 64 MiB extracted source, and a 30 second subprocess deadline; partial trees are cleaned up on every failure path.

issues.title: Define graph diff semantics
issues.problemOutcome: Reviewers need meaningful architectural changes rather than raw JSON differences.
acceptanceCriteria: Diff classifies added and removed nodes and edges, changed nodes and edges, evidence changes, and unresolved diagnostics.
Results are deterministic, and golden fixtures cover each classification.

issues.title: Publish versioned machine-readable diff output
issues.problemOutcome: CI and future integrations need a stable API.
acceptanceCriteria: JSON diff schema contains summary, revision metadata, changes, evidence references, and diagnostics.
Validator and compatibility fixtures exist, and output is stable across repeated runs.

issues.title: Generate a self-contained static HTML report
issues.problemOutcome: Reviewers need a human-readable artifact without running a server.
acceptanceCriteria: Report contains revision summary, changed edges, per-edge evidence, unsupported diagnostics, and tool/schema versions.
It makes no external requests; basic keyboard navigation and semantic headings are tested.
Report generation enforces ceilings of 10,000 nodes, 20,000 edges, 5,000 diagnostics, and 16 MiB output; over-limit reports fail with an actionable diagnostic rather than silently truncating.

issues.title: Stabilize CLI commands, errors, and exit behavior
issues.problemOutcome: Scripts and developers need predictable invocation and failure semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: Supported commands, stdout and stderr rules, JSON mode, configuration errors, analysis errors, and exit codes are documented and tested.
Redaction tests seed tokens, credentials, absolute paths, and source snippets across every error class and prove default logs omit the values while retaining actionable stable diagnostics.

issues.title: Add correctness, determinism, and benchmark regression CI
issues.problemOutcome: New extractors and reports can silently reduce quality or performance.
acceptanceCriteria: CI runs fixture correctness, determinism, schema, and performance checks; a baseline is recorded.
Releases are blocked for evidence or schema regressions or unexplained performance regressions above 20%.

issues.title: Classify edge additions, removals, rewires, and evidence changes
issues.problemOutcome: A raw set difference does not tell reviewers whether an architecture relationship was added, removed, or merely re-evidenced.
acceptanceCriteria: The diff model distinguishes node changes, edge changes, endpoint rewires, evidence-only changes, and confidence changes.
Golden fixtures cover each classification and output remains stable when unrelated graph ordering changes.

issues.title: Compute evidence-backed change impact subgraphs
issues.problemOutcome: Reviewers need a bounded view of what a changed node can reach instead of scanning the entire graph.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic traversal computes configurable forward/reverse impact sets while preserving edge confidence and evidence references.
Cycles, depth limits, and unresolved edges are represented explicitly and benchmarked on a fixture with known reachability.

issues.title: Define merge-base, rebase, and pull-request diff semantics
issues.problemOutcome: Different revision contexts can produce materially different architecture changes if comparison bases are implicit.
acceptanceCriteria: CLI and Action contracts define merge-base selection, shallow-clone failures, rebases, and unrelated histories.
Fixtures cover each mode and record exact Git revisions in diff metadata without fetching implicitly.

issues.title: Ship a read-only GitHub Action with report artifact
issues.problemOutcome: Maintainers need pull-request-level architecture visibility.
acceptanceCriteria: Action analyzes base and head on a pull request, emits a concise summary, and uploads the static report artifact.
An example workflow works on a fixture repository, and initial mode is informational.

issues.title: Harden Action permissions and fork-PR behavior
issues.problemOutcome: CI analysis must not expose secrets or grant write access to untrusted changes.
acceptanceCriteria: Workflow uses least-privilege permissions; fork pull request behavior is documented and tested.
Dependency or action pinning and update policy are documented; no secrets are passed to analyzer processes; actionlint or equivalent checks pass.

issues.title: Establish reproducible package and release pipeline
issues.problemOutcome: Users need trustworthy, repeatable releases.
acceptanceCriteria: Tagging produces an installable package, changelog, checksums or equivalent artifact metadata, and package-install smoke test.
Versioning and rollback guidance are documented, and generated build output is excluded from source commits.

issues.title: Publish quickstart, sample repository, and limitations guide
issues.problemOutcome: A technically correct tool can still fail adoption if its supported boundary is unclear.
acceptanceCriteria: A clean checkout can reach its first report using the quickstart; sample repository demonstrates scan and diff.
Documentation covers privacy, unsupported constructs, configuration, troubleshooting, and Action use; links are checked in CI.

issues.title: Run v0.1 compatibility review with representative repositories
issues.problemOutcome: Fixture success alone does not establish practical usefulness.
acceptanceCriteria: At least three representative public repositories or recorded repository snapshots are analyzed.
A compatibility matrix records supported, unknown, and failed constructs; feedback and follow-up issues are published without exposing source.

issues.title: Rehearse release acceptance and rollback
issues.problemOutcome: A release pipeline is incomplete until maintainers can prove the candidate, detect a bad publication, and recover without improvisation.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned acceptance checklist covers clean installation, representative scans, Action behavior, package contents, signatures or provenance, documentation, and known limitations.
A dry-run rollback or deprecation rehearsal records owners, commands, communication steps, recovery time, and follow-up actions without altering an active release.

issues.title: Enforce report artifact retention and redaction policy
issues.problemOutcome: CI artifacts can outlive the source review context or expose repository paths and metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: The Action documents retention defaults, artifact scope, redaction rules, and an opt-out for sensitive repositories.
A workflow test verifies reports contain no absolute paths, source snippets, tokens, or unbounded payloads.

issues.title: Add package provenance, SBOM, and signing evidence
issues.problemOutcome: A useful OSS analyzer is still unsafe to install if release provenance is opaque.
acceptanceCriteria: Release artifacts include reproducible build metadata, dependency inventory, checksum, and a verifiable provenance statement.
The release workflow fails closed on unsigned or mismatched artifacts and never publishes credentials or source fixtures.

issues.title: Maintain a Node.js and operating-system support matrix
issues.problemOutcome: Compiler and filesystem differences can invalidate architecture evidence across supported environments.
acceptanceCriteria: CI tests the declared Node.js LTS window and macOS/Linux support surface with explicit TypeScript/compiler versions.
Unsupported environments fail with a diagnostic and the matrix is checked against package and Action metadata.

issues.title: Publish npm and standalone CLI distribution contracts
issues.problemOutcome: Adopters need a stable install path that does not depend on a source checkout.
acceptanceCriteria: Package exports, bin entrypoints, Node engine requirements, and offline installation behavior are tested from a packed artifact.
A standalone distribution is either reproducibly produced or explicitly deferred with a decision record; no install path executes target repository code.

issues.title: Implement stable graph identity across refactors
issues.problemOutcome: Path- or line-based identity creates noisy diffs during ordinary refactors.
acceptanceCriteria: Identity rules are deterministic and documented; line moves preserve identity; supported rename and move cases preserve identity.
Ambiguous matches are reported rather than guessed, and identity fixtures pass.

issues.title: Add snapshot and identity migration tooling
issues.problemOutcome: Schema and identity evolution otherwise breaks stored artifacts.
acceptanceCriteria: Older supported snapshots are either migrated or rejected with actionable instructions; migration fixtures cover every supported version.
Default behavior does not destructively overwrite the source artifact, and upgrade documentation exists.

issues.title: Expose identity ambiguity and collision diagnostics
issues.problemOutcome: Stable identity can conceal incorrect matches unless ambiguity, collisions, and fallback behavior are visible to reviewers.
acceptanceCriteria: Stable diagnostic codes distinguish collisions, ambiguous candidates, unsupported renames, and fallback identity paths, with evidence for every candidate considered.
No ambiguous match is silently accepted; fixtures verify deterministic diagnostics and documented reviewer actions.

issues.title: Build property-based identity regression corpus
issues.problemOutcome: A small rename fixture set will miss combinations of moves, aliases, overloads, and duplicate symbols that destabilize identity.
acceptanceCriteria: A bounded generator covers line moves, file moves, supported renames, duplicate names, overloads, path aliases, and ambiguous transformations with declared invariants.
Every minimized failure becomes a deterministic regression fixture, and CI publishes the seed and identity-quality result.

issues.title: Verify identity portability across paths and platforms
issues.problemOutcome: Machine-specific paths, case rules, and separators can make equivalent snapshots appear structurally different.
acceptanceCriteria: Fixtures cover Windows and POSIX separators, case-sensitive and case-insensitive collisions, symlink policy, repository relocation, and Unicode normalization.
Equivalent supported projects produce the same logical identities across the CI platform matrix, while unsafe collisions fail with diagnostics.

issues.title: Publish identity quality benchmark and release gate
issues.problemOutcome: Identity stability needs a measurable quality bar before it can underpin policy and historical analysis.
acceptanceCriteria: Benchmark reports preservation, false-match, ambiguity, and unmatched rates by refactor family on curated and generated cases.
Release thresholds and an exception process are documented; the baseline is reproducible and regressions beyond the threshold block release.

issues.title: Publish snapshot and identity migration matrix
issues.problemOutcome: Long-lived repositories need a controlled path through schema and identity changes.
acceptanceCriteria: A matrix lists supported source/target versions, automatic migrations, manual review gates, and expected evidence loss for each transition.
At least one historical snapshot migrates deterministically and the migration report identifies every changed node or edge identity.

issues.title: Integrate refactor-aware matching into graph diffs
issues.problemOutcome: Stable identity primitives do not help reviewers unless the diff pipeline applies them consistently and explains every refactor match.
acceptanceCriteria: The diff pipeline consumes the P-001 identity contract, path history, and bounded similarity candidates, recording the selected match method and evidence without redefining canonical identity.
Golden rename and move diffs suppress false delete/add pairs, preserve genuinely distinct nodes, and expose ambiguous candidates with stable diagnostic codes.

issues.title: Expose identity confidence and ambiguity explanations
issues.problemOutcome: Users need to know when refactor matching is evidence-backed versus heuristic.
acceptanceCriteria: Each matched identity carries a confidence class, contributing signals, and a stable explanation code.
Reports and machine-readable diffs expose low-confidence matches and never collapse ambiguity into a single silent result.

issues.title: Define a versioned local policy configuration
issues.problemOutcome: Teams need graph constraints without a hosted policy service.
acceptanceCriteria: Local policy schema can express bounded node, edge, and diff constraints; configuration is versioned and validated.
Default behavior is informational; examples cover supported graph types; no remote policy fetching occurs.

issues.title: Implement evidence-linked policy evaluation
issues.problemOutcome: A policy failure is only useful if reviewers can understand and verify it.
acceptanceCriteria: Evaluator handles snapshots and diffs; every violation includes stable IDs, evidence references, reason, and policy rule.
Unsupported inputs follow explicit documented behavior, and results are deterministic.

issues.title: Add informational and enforcing CI modes
issues.problemOutcome: Teams need to adopt policies without being forced into immediate blocking checks.
acceptanceCriteria: Informational mode reports violations and exits successfully; enforce mode returns documented nonzero statuses for violations and tool errors.
Action opt-in behavior is tested, and defaults are explicit.

issues.title: Build policy regression and false-positive evaluation suite
issues.problemOutcome: Policy changes can create noisy or contradictory enforcement.
acceptanceCriteria: Positive and negative fixtures cover each policy rule type; expected outcomes pass 100%.
Explanation and evidence regressions are detected, and baseline false-positive and false-negative counts are published for the suite.

issues.title: Define policy composition, precedence, and conflict semantics
issues.problemOutcome: Multiple policy files become unsafe when inheritance, overrides, and contradictory rules have implicit behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: The versioned contract defines includes, scope, precedence, duplicate rule IDs, override limits, cycles, and contradictory outcomes without remote resolution.
Positive and negative fixtures prove deterministic composition, and every conflict produces an evidence-linked configuration error.

issues.title: Add local expiry-bound policy exceptions
issues.problemOutcome: Teams need a controlled migration path, but permanent or unaudited waivers turn enforcement into theater.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned local exception names the rule, bounded graph scope, rationale, owner, creation date, and mandatory expiry; invalid or expired exceptions never silently suppress findings.
Reports distinguish active, expiring, expired, and malformed exceptions, and fixtures cover precedence with informational and enforcing modes.

issues.title: Summarize cycles and layering violations in diffs
issues.problemOutcome: Reviewers cannot prioritize graph changes when cycles and boundary crossings are buried in individual edges.
acceptanceCriteria: Diff output includes deterministic cycle and configured-layer summaries with links back to contributing edge evidence.
The summarizer never invents a layer assignment and emits an unresolved diagnostic when policy metadata is absent.

issues.title: Define and validate local ADR references
issues.problemOutcome: Architecture decisions drift away from the objects they govern.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned local ADR reference contract identifies file, title/status, and graph IDs.
Missing, stale, and malformed references are detected, and no ADR hosting service is required.

issues.title: Render ADR links and evidence in reports
issues.problemOutcome: Reviewers need decisions and structural changes in the same artifact.
acceptanceCriteria: Static reports show linked ADR title/status and evidence; diffs identify added, removed, and stale references.
The report remains self-contained and deterministic.

issues.title: Document policy and ADR workflows
issues.problemOutcome: Users need a safe adoption path from observation to enforcement.
acceptanceCriteria: Tutorial covers scan, diff, policy, ADR linking, review, migration, and limitations; examples run in CI.
Documentation links are checked, and no claim is made that ADR links prove architectural intent.

issues.title: Model ADR lifecycle and supersession semantics
issues.problemOutcome: A link to an accepted, superseded, rejected, or draft decision should not carry the same architectural meaning.
acceptanceCriteria: The ADR contract defines recognized lifecycle states, supersession links, effective dates, invalid transitions, and behavior for unknown conventions.
Fixtures cover chained supersession, cycles, missing targets, and status changes with deterministic diagnostics.

issues.title: Report decision coverage and reverse references
issues.problemOutcome: Maintainers cannot find ungoverned architecture or assess decision drift from one-way ADR links alone.
acceptanceCriteria: Snapshots and reports provide deterministic ADR-to-graph and graph-to-ADR indexes with coverage counts by supported node and edge kind.
Coverage is explicitly descriptive rather than a compliance score, and tests cover deleted, ambiguous, and many-to-many references.

issues.title: Evaluate policy and decision drift on change scenarios
issues.problemOutcome: Traceability is not proven until real change scenarios reveal stale decisions and policy gaps with tolerable noise.
acceptanceCriteria: A curated scenario suite covers decision supersession, removed architecture, policy changes, unreferenced additions, exceptions, and mixed schema versions.
The evaluation publishes expected and observed drift findings, false-positive categories, reviewer effort, and a documented milestone exit decision.

issues.title: Bind ADR references to policy evaluation
issues.problemOutcome: A policy exception should point to the architectural decision that justifies it, not a free-form comment.
acceptanceCriteria: Policies can require an ADR reference for selected boundaries, exemptions, and planned violations.
Missing, stale, or mismatched ADR references are reported with the graph evidence and never silently accepted.

issues.title: Publish adapter API and capability manifest
issues.problemOutcome: New frameworks should not require core changes or undocumented assumptions.
acceptanceCriteria: Adapter interface covers source/config input, graph output, evidence, diagnostics, capability declaration, and compatibility version.
A sample adapter is documented, and adapter execution rules do not permit arbitrary repository code execution.

issues.title: Build adapter conformance kit and documentation
issues.problemOutcome: An adapter ecosystem without shared quality gates would weaken trust.
acceptanceCriteria: Test kit checks schema validity, determinism, evidence completeness, unsupported diagnostics, identity behavior, and performance.
Sample adapter passes, and versioning and failure semantics are documented.

issues.title: Add one additional TypeScript framework adapter
issues.problemOutcome: Express-only support limits usefulness, but arbitrary framework expansion creates maintenance debt.
acceptanceCriteria: Framework is selected through a public RFC based on demand, semantic fit, testability, and maintainer capacity.
Bounded support is documented; adapter passes conformance and publishes coverage and unknown metrics; core remains unchanged.

issues.title: Enforce adapter isolation and resource budgets
issues.problemOutcome: Third-party adapters expand the untrusted-input and denial-of-service surface of every scan.
acceptanceCriteria: The adapter contract defines filesystem, network, subprocess, time, memory, input-size, and output-size boundaries with fail-closed defaults.
Conformance tests exercise hangs, oversized output, malformed evidence, path escapes, attempted network access, and cleanup after termination.

issues.title: Add adapter compatibility negotiation and migrations
issues.problemOutcome: Core, schema, and adapter version drift otherwise produces opaque failures or silently invalid graphs.
acceptanceCriteria: Capability negotiation reports compatible, migratable, experimental, and rejected combinations before analysis begins.
Compatibility fixtures span every supported core and adapter contract; failure guidance and retirement windows are documented.

issues.title: Ship an adapter starter and maintainer review playbook
issues.problemOutcome: An interface alone does not make safe external adapter contributions repeatable or reviewable.
acceptanceCriteria: A minimal starter includes capability declaration, fixtures, conformance, packaging, diagnostics, security boundaries, and compatibility tests that run in CI.
The review playbook defines evidence, quality, ownership, maintenance, security response, and graduation requirements; one independent dry run is recorded.

issues.title: Represent async jobs, event emitters, and callback edges
issues.problemOutcome: Important architecture boundaries are missed when work is scheduled through events or callbacks.
acceptanceCriteria: Documented EventEmitter, queue registration, and callback-passing patterns emit edge kinds that preserve registration and handler evidence.
Dynamic event names, string-only reflection, and unsupported queue clients produce stable unknown diagnostics rather than guessed edges.

issues.title: Separate language-neutral graph semantics from adapters
issues.problemOutcome: Language-specific assumptions would make later language support brittle.
acceptanceCriteria: IR, identity, source mapping, evidence, and unknown semantics are documented independently of TypeScript.
Compatibility fixtures cover language metadata and source coordinates, and existing adapters remain valid.

issues.title: Publish adapter selection criteria and support matrix
issues.problemOutcome: Community demand must determine expansion rather than maintainers guessing at the next framework or language.
acceptanceCriteria: Public RFC defines selection criteria, support expectations, ownership, and retirement rules.
Support matrix identifies implemented, experimental, deferred, and unsupported adapters; an explicit defer decision is acceptable.

issues.title: Pilot one bounded non-TypeScript adapter
issues.problemOutcome: Language expansion should be evidence-based and limited to constructs the project can evaluate.
acceptanceCriteria: One language is selected through the published criteria; only a bounded high-value construct set is supported.
Adapter passes conformance, unsupported categories and precision/recall are reported, and no broad language-support claim is made.

issues.title: Build a cross-language semantic equivalence corpus
issues.problemOutcome: A shared graph vocabulary can hide language-specific differences unless equivalent and non-equivalent constructs are evaluated explicitly.
acceptanceCriteria: The corpus pairs supported TypeScript and pilot-language constructs for modules, calls, routes or boundaries, identity, evidence, and unknown behavior.
Expected equivalences and intentional differences are versioned; conformance reports disagreements by semantic category.

issues.title: Define adapter retirement and security-response policy
issues.problemOutcome: Experimental and community adapters need an honest path to deprecation when quality, ownership, or security support disappears.
acceptanceCriteria: Policy defines ownership, vulnerability intake, supported-version windows, quality regression triggers, deprecation notice, archive behavior, and replacement guidance.
A tabletop exercise covers an abandoned adapter and a security defect, producing timed actions and public communication templates.

issues.title: Publish the language-expansion gate report
issues.problemOutcome: The pilot must end in a transparent continue, narrow, or defer decision rather than an indefinite experimental claim.
acceptanceCriteria: The report compares conformance, semantic coverage, unknown rate, precision and recall, performance, maintenance cost, demand, and security ownership against predeclared thresholds.
A public ADR chooses graduate, retain as experimental, narrow, or retire; rejected expansion creates no implementation commitments.

issues.title: Run adapter compatibility matrix in CI
issues.problemOutcome: Adapters drift against core schema and compiler/runtime versions without shared evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: CI executes every declared adapter against capability fixtures, supported Node/compiler versions, and schema compatibility checks.
Failures identify adapter, capability, fixture, and compatibility dimension; unsupported combinations are declared rather than skipped silently.

issues.title: Add local OpenTelemetry import contract
issues.problemOutcome: Static graphs cannot explain which declared paths are actually observed at runtime.
acceptanceCriteria: At least one documented local OpenTelemetry export format is accepted; spans are normalized into a versioned input contract.
No collector, upload, or network access is required, and invalid input fails safely.

issues.title: Implement static/runtime edge reconciliation
issues.problemOutcome: Users need a cautious distinction between modeled, observed, unobserved, and ambiguous behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Reconciliation classifies observed-and-modeled, modeled-not-observed, observed-but-unmodeled, and ambiguous edges.
Results are deterministic; each classification points to static evidence and trace provenance; uncertainty is explicit.

issues.title: Add runtime data redaction and retention controls
issues.problemOutcome: Trace data may contain secrets, identifiers, headers, or request bodies.
acceptanceCriteria: Runtime reconciliation is opt-in; default processing excludes payloads, headers, and arbitrary attributes.
Configurable redaction and retention behavior is documented; negative tests verify no sensitive values enter snapshots or reports; threat model is updated.

issues.title: Evaluate runtime reconciliation on synthetic traces
issues.problemOutcome: Runtime matching can appear useful while producing misleading classifications.
acceptanceCriteria: Synthetic traces have known expected classifications; precision, recall, coverage, and ambiguity are reported.
Limitations and sampling caveats are documented; release gating is not enabled until the baseline is reviewed.

issues.title: Model sampling, clock, and service-identity uncertainty
issues.problemOutcome: Trace sampling, clock skew, aliases, and missing propagation can make absence or correlation look more certain than the data permits.
acceptanceCriteria: The reconciliation contract represents sampling metadata, time uncertainty, service aliases, missing parents, and confidence without treating unobserved behavior as absent.
Synthetic fixtures vary sampling and clock conditions; reports explain which classifications changed and why.

issues.title: Integrate explicit opt-in local runtime reconciliation
issues.problemOutcome: Runtime evidence is usable only when users opt in locally and can distinguish observations from static architecture claims.
acceptanceCriteria: CLI and reports accept only explicit local inputs, keep static and runtime provenance separate, expose uncertainty and diagnostics, and never require a collector, upload, credential, source payload, or network path.
Input count, bytes, processing time, output cardinality, and retention are bounded; end-to-end tests prove offline execution, redaction, and fail-closed over-limit behavior.

issues.title: Classify static/runtime coverage and disagreement
issues.problemOutcome: A runtime observation must not be mistaken for proof that an unobserved static edge does not exist.
acceptanceCriteria: Reports distinguish statically known/runtime observed, statically known/unobserved, runtime-only, and ambiguous relationships.
Classification is deterministic for a fixed input and includes sampling, revision, and capability limitations.

issues.title: Build a local runtime reconciliation fixture corpus
issues.problemOutcome: Runtime reconciliation needs controlled examples before any external data is considered.
acceptanceCriteria: Fixtures cover HTTP, database, messaging, errors, missing parents, sampling, redaction, and static/runtime disagreement.
Each fixture has provenance, expected classifications, and a digest-only result that runs without network or exporter access.

issues.title: Enforce runtime sampling and cost budgets
issues.problemOutcome: Optional runtime evidence can become an unbounded storage and review burden.
acceptanceCriteria: Import limits spans, attributes, trace count, analysis time, and report size with stable fail-closed diagnostics.
Budget fixtures prove deterministic truncation is never reported as complete coverage and redacted data is not retained in temp files.

issues.title: Establish large-repository performance budgets
issues.problemOutcome: A useful analyzer becomes unusable if scan time or memory grows unpredictably.
acceptanceCriteria: Small, medium, and large benchmark tiers are defined; p95 runtime, peak memory, report size, and fixture results are recorded.
No unexplained regression above 20% is accepted between releases.

issues.title: Add bounded fuzz/property and security regression testing
issues.problemOutcome: Parsers, JSON snapshots, policy files, and adapters process untrusted input.
acceptanceCriteria: Bounded fuzz or property suites cover TypeScript input, snapshot JSON, policy configuration, and adapter output.
Every discovered crash or security defect becomes a regression fixture, and CI has an explicit runtime budget.

issues.title: Publish compatibility, upgrade, and maintenance policy
issues.problemOutcome: Users need to know what is supported and how schema or adapter changes are handled.
acceptanceCriteria: Supported runtime and OS policy, semantic-versioning rules, deprecation policy, snapshot/policy/adapter compatibility, upgrade guidance, and maintenance ownership are documented.
CI cross-checks package engine declarations, the workflow runtime matrix, and schema and adapter compatibility versions against the published support and upgrade documentation, failing on drift.

issues.title: Create a public adopter and contributor feedback loop
issues.problemOutcome: The roadmap should reflect observed user value and community capacity.
acceptanceCriteria: Public RFC process, issue triage taxonomy, adopter feedback template, and anonymized feedback summary exist.
Feedback produces explicit backlog decisions, and no source or private telemetry is required.

issues.title: Automate the release compatibility matrix
issues.problemOutcome: Manual compatibility claims drift from the versions and migrations that releases actually exercise.
acceptanceCriteria: CI tests supported Node, operating-system, snapshot, policy, adapter, and Action-version combinations from a machine-readable matrix.
Documentation is generated or checked against the matrix, unsupported combinations fail clearly, and every release records the tested set.

issues.title: Reduce contributor and maintainer single points of failure
issues.problemOutcome: A technically mature project remains fragile when triage, releases, adapters, and security response depend on one maintainer.
acceptanceCriteria: Ownership and onboarding maps cover triage, release, security, core contracts, adapters, and roadmap operations with documented backup paths.
At least two non-author dry runs complete a representative contribution and release-or-triage task; friction and unresolved bus-factor risks are published.

issues.title: Govern the benchmark corpus and measurement protocol
issues.problemOutcome: Performance and accuracy claims drift when inputs and measurement methods change silently.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned protocol defines fixture selection, warm/cold runs, hardware/runtime disclosure, accuracy denominators, and acceptable variance.
Benchmark artifacts record corpus digests and tool versions without including source bodies or hidden telemetry.

issues.title: Expand offline Action fixtures and fork-security regression tests
issues.problemOutcome: Workflow changes can accidentally introduce token exposure or execute repository-controlled code.
acceptanceCriteria: Fixtures cover fork pull requests, malicious package scripts, symlinked outputs, oversized inputs, cancellation, and missing refs.
The workflow policy test rejects write permissions, pull_request_target, unpinned actions, and secret-dependent analysis paths.

issues.title: Publish an OSS health and traction scorecard
issues.problemOutcome: Hosted or team investment must not be justified by vanity metrics or assumptions.
acceptanceCriteria: Scorecard defines external repositories with successful runs, repeat non-maintainer contributors, release stability, issue quality, maintainer load, security history, and retention or feedback measures.
Collection is transparent and does not add hidden telemetry.

issues.title: Record the local-first investment boundary
issues.problemOutcome: The project needs an explicit boundary that protects a complete local-first OSS product from speculative hosted or team scope.
acceptanceCriteria: A public ADR chooses local-first OSS stewardship or authorizes only a separate discovery phase backed by explicit traction, privacy, security, capacity, and funding evidence.
No account, source upload, hidden telemetry, hosted implementation, or required network path is added unless a later reviewed gate and separate ADR authorize it.

issues.title: Run the strategy-branch privacy and security review
issues.problemOutcome: Any team or hosted direction changes trust boundaries and cannot inherit the local-only threat model by assumption.
acceptanceCriteria: The selected branch has updated assets, actors, data flows, tenancy and authorization assumptions, retention, incident response, supply-chain risks, and abuse cases.
A public summary names blocking mitigations and rejected data collection; an OSS-only decision records why no new boundary is needed.

issues.title: Publish a sustainability and cost model
issues.problemOutcome: Roadmap scope must reflect the real maintenance, support, CI, release, security, and infrastructure cost of each strategy branch.
acceptanceCriteria: The model estimates maintainer hours, CI and artifact cost, dependency upkeep, support burden, security response, adapter ownership, and any approved service operations with ranges and assumptions.
Funding and scope options identify break-even or stop conditions without treating volunteer labor as free.

issues.title: Audit Year 1–3 claims against shipped evidence
issues.problemOutcome: The first strategy gate needs an evidence-based audit of claims made during the first three program years before later investment is authorized.
acceptanceCriteria: A public audit maps every material Year 1–3 capability, quality, privacy, adoption, and maintenance claim to reproducible repository or release evidence.
Unsupported, partial, or negative results are labeled plainly and feed the Year 4 charter instead of being converted into roadmap-completion claims.

issues.title: Charter the conditional Year 4 investment
issues.problemOutcome: Later roadmap items should begin only with explicit capacity, evidence, and branch-specific boundaries.
acceptanceCriteria: A public charter selects funded team-scale work, OSS-only hardening, or a maintenance track; it names outcomes, owners, capacity, non-goals, risks, and quarter-level stop conditions.
Year 4 expansion remains deferred unless the strategy, security, sustainability, and claims-audit gates are accepted.

issues.title: Publish repository adoption evaluation reports
issues.problemOutcome: Adoption claims need reproducible evaluation evidence about supported repositories, not screenshots, vanity counts, certifications, or support guarantees.
acceptanceCriteria: An evaluation template records repository size, languages and frameworks, scan revision, coverage and unknowns, timing, reviewer usefulness, and explicit limitations without implying certification or a support guarantee.
At least three external or public fixtures are rerunnable from pinned revisions without collecting source, credentials, hidden telemetry, or user data.

issues.title: Define telemetry-free adoption measurement
issues.problemOutcome: The project needs adoption evidence without introducing undisclosed collection or weakening local-first guarantees.
acceptanceCriteria: Metrics rely on opt-in public reports, issue templates, release metadata, and manually reproducible repository runs; hidden telemetry is prohibited.
The protocol documents sampling bias, retention, anonymization, and deletion responsibilities.

issues.title: Define a versioned architecture query contract
issues.problemOutcome: Impact and architecture questions need a stable contract before adding a query interface or claiming useful answers.
acceptanceCriteria: The contract defines bounded selectors, node and edge predicates, traversal limits, result ordering, evidence projection, diagnostics, schema version, and unsupported operations.
Queries are local, read-only, deterministic, resource-bounded, and validated against positive, negative, malformed, and over-limit fixtures.

issues.title: Implement bounded reachability and dependency-path queries
issues.problemOutcome: Reviewers need to trace how architecture objects connect without exporting the graph into ad hoc scripts.
acceptanceCriteria: Queries support direct neighbors, bounded upstream and downstream reachability, shortest dependency paths, boundary crossing, and cycle reporting over declared edge kinds.
Results have canonical ordering, complete evidence links, explicit truncation diagnostics, and benchmarked node, edge, depth, time, and output ceilings.

issues.title: Add policy, decision, and ownership query projections
issues.problemOutcome: Structural paths alone do not tell reviewers which controls, decisions, or maintainers govern the affected architecture.
acceptanceCriteria: Query results can project applicable policy rules and findings, ADR references and status, declared ownership hints, exceptions, and unsupported metadata without changing evaluation semantics.
Missing, conflicting, and stale metadata remains visible; fixtures verify that projections preserve source provenance and do not infer absent ownership.

issues.title: Model evidence-backed change-impact scenarios
issues.problemOutcome: A changed node may affect callers, policies, routes, decisions, and runtime observations, but unrestricted transitive reachability overstates risk.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned impact model defines supported change kinds, traversal rules, boundary stops, confidence, unknowns, and reasons for inclusion across curated scenarios.
Golden evaluations report expected affected sets, precision, recall, overreach categories, and reviewer-visible uncertainty rather than a single opaque risk score.

issues.title: Render inspectable query and impact explanations
issues.problemOutcome: Query output is not decision-grade when reviewers cannot inspect the path, evidence, rule, or uncertainty behind each result.
acceptanceCriteria: JSON and static reports show query text or normalized plan, result path, edge kinds, evidence, applicable policy and ADR context, uncertainty, limits, and tool versions.
Explanations are self-contained, keyboard accessible, stable across repeated runs, and tested against cycles, truncation, missing evidence, and empty results.

issues.title: Publish the architecture-query quality and safety gate
issues.problemOutcome: New query features should not proceed to team-scale composition until correctness, performance, and reviewer utility are measured.
acceptanceCriteria: Evaluation covers deterministic correctness, impact precision and recall, explanation completeness, worst-case resource behavior, malformed inputs, path leakage, and reviewer task completion on representative scenarios.
A public gate report compares predeclared thresholds, lists failures and limitations, and records continue, narrow, or defer decisions for multi-repository work.

issues.title: Detect workspace package boundaries and ownership
issues.problemOutcome: Monorepo architecture reviews need package-level ownership without guessing from directory names.
acceptanceCriteria: npm, pnpm, Yarn, and documented workspace manifests produce package nodes with stable root evidence and dependency edges.
Overlapping or malformed workspace declarations fail with actionable diagnostics and never merge unrelated package roots.

issues.title: Extract bounded GraphQL and REST schema boundaries
issues.problemOutcome: API contracts can drift from implementation while module-only graphs look unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: Supported GraphQL schema/resolver and OpenAPI-to-handler references produce evidence-linked boundary nodes.
Schema generation, aliases, and runtime-composed routes are reported as partial coverage with stable diagnostic codes.

issues.title: Extract Prisma schema and generated-client relationships
issues.problemOutcome: Database models and service boundaries remain invisible when generated clients are excluded without provenance.
acceptanceCriteria: Prisma datasource, model, relation, and generated-client references map to typed graph nodes with schema-file evidence.
Multiple schema files, unsupported providers, and generated output paths are classified explicitly; no database connection or generation command runs.

issues.title: Model lockfiles and package-manager dependency edges
issues.problemOutcome: Architecture review lacks reproducible package provenance when it reads only source imports.
acceptanceCriteria: Supported npm, pnpm, Yarn, and Bun lockfile records are normalized into optional dependency evidence without resolving the network.
Lockfile version mismatches and integrity omissions produce diagnostics; source graph output remains deterministic offline.

issues.title: Track generated-code provenance and exclusion diagnostics
issues.problemOutcome: Ignoring generated code can hide important boundaries or mislead users about what was analyzed.
acceptanceCriteria: Generated files are classified by configured and detected provenance, with source-to-generated relationships where evidence is available.
Reports state exactly which generated paths were excluded and why; generated fixtures prove no silent omission.

issues.title: Benchmark diffs on bounded large-graph workloads
issues.problemOutcome: Scale claims are credible only when they are tied to reproducible declared workload tiers and explicit resource ceilings.
acceptanceCriteria: Generated benchmarks declare graph cardinality, edge density, identity ambiguity, wall time, peak memory, report size, and hardware context for each supported workload tier.
CI enforces documented budgets with an allowed variance band, retains digest-only evidence, and fails closed when an input exceeds a declared supported tier.

issues.title: Add deterministic query pagination and result budgets
issues.problemOutcome: Architecture queries become unusable when a broad selector returns an unbounded result set.
acceptanceCriteria: Query results support stable cursors, explicit cardinality limits, and a machine-readable truncated state.
Repeated queries over the same canonical graph return byte-identical pages and never silently discard matches.

issues.title: Define the offline workspace composition contract
issues.problemOutcome: Multi-repository analysis needs an explicit local boundary for inputs, versions, trust, and missing repositories before graphs can be combined.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned workspace manifest identifies repository snapshots, logical names, revisions, schema and adapter versions, optional boundaries, local paths, and declared omissions without embedding source.
Validation rejects duplicate identities, incompatible versions, path escapes, unbounded inputs, and implicit network fetches; minimal and mixed-version fixtures pass.

issues.title: Implement cross-repository identity namespaces
issues.problemOutcome: Independently valid snapshots can collide or become unstable when repository names, relocations, forks, and revisions enter one workspace.
acceptanceCriteria: Composed identities include stable repository namespace semantics with explicit behavior for relocation, forks, aliases, duplicate origins, and unavailable origin metadata.
Property and portability tests prove deterministic identity, surface ambiguity, and preserve each underlying snapshot without destructive rewriting.

issues.title: Resolve declared cross-repository boundaries and dependencies
issues.problemOutcome: Portfolio graphs are misleading if package, service, schema, or runtime relationships are guessed from names or silently left disconnected.
acceptanceCriteria: A bounded resolver supports declared package and service references plus explicitly selected evidence sources, distinguishing resolved, ambiguous, external, unavailable, and unsupported relationships.
Every cross-repository edge includes provenance from both sides or an unresolved reason; fixtures cover version skew, aliases, monorepos, cycles, and missing repositories.

issues.title: Add provenance-aware incremental workspace recomposition
issues.problemOutcome: Rebuilding an entire portfolio after one snapshot changes wastes time, while stale cache reuse can corrupt decisions.
acceptanceCriteria: Cache keys cover content, contract, adapter, policy, workspace, and tool versions; changed inputs invalidate only proven dependents and never bypass validation.
Cold, warm, partial-change, corrupt-cache, and interrupted-run tests prove byte-identical results, atomic updates, cleanup, and measured speedup.

issues.title: Enforce workspace privacy and resource boundaries
issues.problemOutcome: Composing multiple repositories multiplies source-path leakage, sensitive metadata, denial-of-service, and accidental data-sharing risk.
acceptanceCriteria: The threat model and defaults bound repository count, aggregate nodes and edges, bytes, depth, time, memory, cache, report size, path exposure, and optional runtime metadata.
Negative tests cover malicious manifests, symlink escapes, decompression and graph bombs, secret-bearing metadata, mixed trust, partial failure, and guaranteed temporary-data cleanup.

issues.title: Evaluate federation on representative repository portfolios
issues.problemOutcome: A multi-repository feature needs evidence that composition improves real review tasks without unacceptable noise or cost.
acceptanceCriteria: At least three reproducible public or sanitized portfolios exercise package, service, schema, missing-repository, version-skew, and cross-boundary change scenarios at declared size tiers.
The report publishes resolution precision and recall, unknown coverage, identity stability, incremental performance, reviewer usefulness, privacy findings, and a graduate, narrow, or defer decision.

issues.title: Implement a SCIP import and export contract
issues.problemOutcome: Existing language indexers can provide useful evidence, but interchange must not erase CARTOGRAPH semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: SCIP symbols and relationships map to canonical references with index/tool/version provenance and no raw source payload.
Round-trip fixtures preserve stable identity/evidence references and explicitly mark fields SCIP cannot represent.

issues.title: Resolve architecture ownership from explicit local sources
issues.problemOutcome: Findings cannot enter a reliable review workflow when ownership is guessed from contributor history or a single unmatched path rule.
acceptanceCriteria: Resolution combines versioned local ownership rules and supported CODEOWNERS semantics with documented precedence, team aliases, fallback, conflicts, and unavailable owners.
Every result cites the matching rule and source; fixtures cover nested patterns, negation limits, renamed paths, cross-repository objects, ambiguity, and no-owner outcomes.

issues.title: Define an auditable finding lifecycle
issues.problemOutcome: Open, acknowledged, remediated, waived, regressed, and obsolete findings need stable semantics across scans and releases.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned local lifecycle contract defines finding identity, allowed states and transitions, actor, timestamp, rationale, evidence revision, supersession, and invalid-state behavior.
Transition replay is deterministic and append-only; fixtures cover identity migration, concurrent records, policy changes, removed architecture, regression, and tampering.

issues.title: Add locally verifiable, expiry-bound architecture waivers
issues.problemOutcome: Architecture exceptions need bounded local provenance and expiry without implying that signatures or waivers confer authority.
acceptanceCriteria: The waiver schema binds rule and change scope, rationale, owner, approver, creation, expiry, evidence revision, optional signature metadata, and explicit local trust roots without storing private keys.
Verification is offline; unsigned, invalid, broadened, replayed, revoked, and expired waivers stay visible and cannot suppress enforcement, and a waiver never grants authority by itself.

issues.title: Detect ownership and exception drift
issues.problemOutcome: Renames, team changes, policy evolution, and time can leave findings assigned to nobody or hidden behind obsolete exceptions.
acceptanceCriteria: Analysis detects owner disappearance, ambiguous reassignment, scope drift, approaching and passed expiry, invalid signatures, changed evidence, and policy-version mismatch with stable diagnostic codes.
Reports preserve the prior decision trail, never auto-extend an exception, and fixtures cover repository moves, policy migration, key rotation, and partial workspaces.

issues.title: Integrate ownership and finding state into review outputs
issues.problemOutcome: Reviewers need one bounded summary of new, changed, accepted, expired, and ownerless findings without exposing secrets or requiring write permissions.
acceptanceCriteria: CLI, JSON, static report, and read-only Action show lifecycle change, owner source, waiver validity, evidence, policy and ADR context, due or expiry state, and actionable next steps.
Fork and least-privilege tests prove no untrusted code gains signing material or write access; summaries have cardinality limits and link to full local artifacts.

issues.title: Evaluate review workflow usability, integrity, and load
issues.problemOutcome: Workflow features can add ceremony, concentrate approval power, or create a false audit trail without improving architecture decisions.
acceptanceCriteria: A study measures triage accuracy, time-to-owner, waiver review time, stale-finding rate, reviewer task completion, maintainer load, and failure recovery on representative scenarios.
Security review covers forgery, replay, broad waivers, owner spoofing, fork pull requests, and compromised keys; a public gate records graduate, narrow, redesign, or defer outcomes.

issues.title: Add patch-scoped graph and policy filtering
issues.problemOutcome: Large pull requests need a bounded review without losing the ability to inspect full evidence on demand.
acceptanceCriteria: A patch filter selects changed-file evidence plus configurable one-hop context and reports omitted graph regions.
Filtering is deterministic, cannot turn a policy violation into a pass, and has fixtures for renames and generated files.

issues.title: Define a deterministic graph and diff query language
issues.problemOutcome: Ad hoc filters cannot be reused in reports, CI, and editor integrations.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned query grammar supports node/edge kinds, evidence paths, confidence, revision changes, and bounded traversal.
Parser errors are stable, query execution has resource limits, and equivalent queries produce canonical selections.

issues.title: Render filtered graph views without misleading layout semantics
issues.problemOutcome: Visual maps can imply proximity or completeness that the underlying evidence does not support.
acceptanceCriteria: A local report renders selected nodes and typed edges with legends for confidence, unresolved edges, and omitted context.
Layout is deterministic for the same canonical input and tests verify that visual grouping never changes graph semantics.

issues.title: Publish portable graph interchange exports
issues.problemOutcome: Users need to consume canonical architecture evidence without adopting CARTOGRAPH's renderer.
acceptanceCriteria: Versioned JSON, JSON-LD, and a documented edge-list export preserve IDs, evidence references, confidence, and unresolved reasons.
Round-trip fixtures prove exports do not invent edges or drop required provenance, and unsupported fields fail visibly.

issues.title: Meet accessibility and keyboard-navigation requirements for reports
issues.problemOutcome: A graph review surface is not useful if its evidence and changes are inaccessible to keyboard or assistive-technology users.
acceptanceCriteria: HTML reports provide semantic tables/details alternatives, focus order, keyboard navigation, reduced-motion behavior, and visible status text.
Automated accessibility checks plus a manual fixture review cover changed nodes, diagnostics, and evidence links.

issues.title: Publish pull-request check summaries and source annotations
issues.problemOutcome: A report artifact alone makes architecture changes hard to triage during review.
acceptanceCriteria: The Action emits a bounded check summary with counts, confidence, unresolved diagnostics, and links to an artifact.
Line annotations are evidence-backed, capped, and never expose source bodies or absolute paths; fork permissions are tested.

issues.title: Define a bounded SARIF policy-result bridge
issues.problemOutcome: Policy findings need to interoperate with code-scanning surfaces without misrepresenting graph evidence as vulnerability analysis.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned export maps only line-local policy violations to SARIF and retains canonical graph/evidence IDs as references.
Import/export fixtures reject unsupported result kinds, source bodies, and missing fingerprints; documentation states the boundary clearly.

issues.title: Support evidence-path and source-span query predicates
issues.problemOutcome: Reviewers need to query architecture changes by where evidence lives, not only by graph kind.
acceptanceCriteria: The query contract supports normalized repository paths, spans, extractor versions, confidence, and unresolved reasons.
Fixtures prove path traversal, absolute paths, and malformed spans are rejected while valid predicates remain cross-platform deterministic.

issues.title: Add query regression and authorization-boundary fixtures
issues.problemOutcome: Reusable queries must not bypass policy or expose paths outside the selected repository.
acceptanceCriteria: Regression fixtures cover query parser bugs, path containment, policy-filtered results, and stale snapshot references.
The evaluator proves query output cannot grant or change policy decisions and remains bounded under adversarial selectors.

issues.title: Define a reproducible architecture assurance bundle
issues.problemOutcome: Teams need a portable explanation of what was analyzed and controlled, but a report alone does not preserve all inputs, contracts, and limits required for replay.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned bundle manifest references snapshots, diffs, policies, decisions, lifecycle records, waivers, query results, tool and adapter versions, configurations, limits, and generated reports without requiring source inclusion.
Canonical packaging, size ceilings, media types, missing-artifact semantics, and offline validation are specified; repeated exports from identical inputs are byte-identical.

issues.title: Sign assurance manifests and verify artifact provenance
issues.problemOutcome: Recipients cannot trust a portable evidence bundle when integrity, producer identity, and artifact relationships are unverifiable.
acceptanceCriteria: The bundle records content digests, build and tool provenance, signing identity metadata, timestamp policy, and verification results using documented interoperable mechanisms.
Offline verification detects missing, altered, substituted, expired, revoked, and unsupported artifacts; private keys never enter CARTOGRAPH configuration or reports.

issues.title: Link architecture evidence to SBOM and build provenance
issues.problemOutcome: Source architecture findings and released software inventory remain disconnected when packages, builds, and graph identities cannot be reconciled cautiously.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned mapping accepts selected SPDX or CycloneDX and build-provenance inputs, relating supported components and artifacts to graph objects with evidence, confidence, and unresolved reasons.
Fixtures cover aliases, bundled outputs, generated code, missing packages, version skew, malformed input, and ambiguous mappings; no completeness claim is made beyond measured coverage.

issues.title: Map architecture controls to evidence without compliance claims
issues.problemOutcome: Control owners need traceable evidence, while presenting architecture checks as certification would mislead users and auditors.
acceptanceCriteria: A local mapping contract links named control objectives to policies, findings, decisions, owners, waivers, tests, and bundle artifacts with scope, period, status, and evidence gaps.
Reports separate observed evidence from owner assertions, include prominent non-certification limitations, and test stale, conflicting, missing, and partially applicable mappings.

issues.title: Harden local assurance redaction, retention, and safe sharing
issues.problemOutcome: Portable local bundles can combine sensitive repository names, paths, findings, decisions, and runtime metadata even without a hosted service.
acceptanceCriteria: The local and offline threat model defines default exclusions, field-level redaction, pseudonymization limits, recipient profiles, retention, deletion, and safe-sharing checks without implying centralized access control or compliance certification.
Leakage tests seed secrets and identifiers across every artifact type; unsafe exports fail closed without echoing sensitive values and do not require a hosted encryption or authorization service.

issues.title: Prove independent assurance-bundle replay
issues.problemOutcome: An assurance format is not credible until a separate environment can validate and reproduce its declared results within documented limits.
acceptanceCriteria: A clean, network-disabled environment verifies signatures and digests, validates contracts, regenerates derived reports, and compares deterministic outputs using only the declared bundle and public tooling.
At least one independent reviewer follows the replay guide; discrepancies, portability failures, redaction findings, time and resource use, and the milestone gate decision are published.

issues.title: Add content-addressed CI cache keys
issues.problemOutcome: Repeated scans are slow, but unsound cache reuse can produce stale architecture evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Cache keys bind tool version, config digest, revision, lockfile digest, and relevant source inputs without storing source bodies remotely.
Cache-hit and invalidation fixtures prove changed configuration or dependencies cannot reuse incompatible snapshots.

issues.title: Define a versioned local architecture history store
issues.problemOutcome: Longitudinal analysis needs durable, migratable records rather than an unbounded directory of unrelated snapshots and reports.
acceptanceCriteria: The local store indexes revisions, snapshots, diffs, policies, decisions, finding lifecycles, workspace composition, provenance, and schema versions using content-addressed immutable records and explicit references.
Atomic import, deduplication, validation, corruption detection, migration, export, and recovery are specified; no network service or hidden telemetry is required.

issues.title: Implement reproducible architecture trend metrics
issues.problemOutcome: Teams need to see structural evolution, but raw graph size and finding counts can reward growth or hide quality changes.
acceptanceCriteria: Versioned metrics cover supported boundary changes, dependency direction, cycles, policy findings, decision coverage, ownership, waivers, unknowns, runtime reconciliation, and churn with denominators and scope.
Every metric can be recomputed from stored evidence, records contract and configuration versions, and is tested against no-change, rename, missing-history, and schema-migration scenarios.

issues.title: Represent history gaps, baseline changes, and uncertainty
issues.problemOutcome: Trends become misleading when missing revisions, changed extractors, altered policies, or incomplete workspaces are plotted as comparable observations.
acceptanceCriteria: History marks missing periods, partial snapshots, contract and adapter changes, policy changes, workspace-scope changes, migrations, sampling changes, and incomparable metrics with machine-readable reasons.
Reports never interpolate or rank incomparable values by default; synthetic timelines verify uncertainty bands, breaks, restatements, and reviewer explanations.

issues.title: Track evidence-backed architecture debt indicators
issues.problemOutcome: Transparent indicators can show aging or recurring architecture findings without inventing predictive debt scores or business outcomes.
acceptanceCriteria: Supported indicators cover finding age, recurrence, waiver history, ownership gaps, policy severity, boundary erosion, unknown coverage, and remediation evidence without predicting debt or business outcomes.
Definitions and thresholds are configurable and versioned; counterexamples, uncertainty, sensitivity, and per-indicator evidence are published on curated timelines.

issues.title: Add history retention, compaction, and selective export
issues.problemOutcome: Long-lived architecture evidence can grow without bound and retain sensitive metadata beyond its useful or permitted lifetime.
acceptanceCriteria: Policy controls retention by artifact and classification, legal or owner hold metadata, safe compaction, tombstones, garbage collection, export scope, and documented irreversibility without silently breaking referenced evidence.
Tests cover boundary dates, shared content, failed compaction, corrupt indexes, deletion verification, migrated records, redacted export, and deterministic rebuild of retained metrics.

issues.title: Evaluate longitudinal validity, performance, and usefulness
issues.problemOutcome: History features should not graduate unless their metrics survive migrations, gaps, scale, and real maintainer interpretation.
acceptanceCriteria: Evaluation uses synthetic ground truth and representative multi-version repositories to measure metric reproducibility, false trend signals, migration equivalence, query latency, storage growth, compaction, and reviewer task accuracy.
A public report documents privacy and retention findings, sensitivity limits, decision usefulness, rejected metrics, and a graduate, narrow, or defer gate for remediation assistance.

issues.title: Review the secure boundary for optional local export/import
issues.problemOutcome: Optional handoff can expand identity, authorization, and retention risk even when CARTOGRAPH remains local and offline.
acceptanceCriteria: A threat-model review defines bounded local export and import, identity, authorization, retention, conflict handling, integrity checks, and no-network defaults.
The review covers only local and offline handoff; any account, hosted service, or required network workflow needs a later independent ADR and security gate.

issues.title: Analyze longitudinal ownership and waiver churn
issues.problemOutcome: Point-in-time drift diagnostics do not show whether ownership gaps and exception reuse are recurring, improving, or artifacts of missing history.
acceptanceCriteria: Versioned historical analysis measures owner changes, gap recurrence, waiver renewal and expiry, scope growth, and review latency without collapsing them into a single score.
