Every trend links to revision evidence and distinguishes missing or migrated history from a verified negative result and from current-state drift findings.

issues.title: Define a governed remediation suggestion contract
issues.problemOutcome: Architecture findings need bounded, inspectable remediation semantics before any system proposes code, policy, decision, or workflow changes.
acceptanceCriteria: The versioned contract distinguishes explanation, investigation step, configuration change, policy or waiver action, documentation action, and code-change suggestion with inputs, evidence, confidence, assumptions, risk, and validation plan.
Unsupported findings produce no fabricated remediation; generation is opt-in, read-only by default, resource-bounded, and tested against stale, ambiguous, ownerless, and security-sensitive cases.

issues.title: Implement deterministic rule-based remediation suggestions
issues.problemOutcome: High-confidence recurring findings can receive useful guidance without introducing probabilistic providers or hidden data flows.
acceptanceCriteria: A reviewed ruleset generates evidence-linked suggestions for a bounded set of policy, configuration, decision-reference, ownership, exception, and supported dependency findings.
Each rule declares applicability, preconditions, non-goals, risk, validation commands, and golden positive and negative fixtures; output is byte-stable and never edits files.

issues.title: Add isolated patch preview, validation, and rollback
issues.problemOutcome: Code-oriented suggestions remain unsafe unless proposed changes can be inspected and tested without mutating the user's working tree or selecting arbitrary commands.
acceptanceCriteria: Patch previews run in an isolated bounded worktree, preserve the original tree, show exact provenance, and require explicit user application outside CARTOGRAPH's default flow.

Validation uses only built-in or maintainer-configured allowlisted non-network commands; repository files cannot select commands or credentials, and tests cover dirty trees, conflicts, malicious inputs, cleanup, and rollback instructions.

issues.title: Specify an optional model-provider privacy boundary
issues.problemOutcome: Probabilistic assistance would create new disclosure, prompt-injection, provenance, reproducibility, and provider-dependence risks that must be designed before integration.
acceptanceCriteria: A public RFC defines local-only and provider-backed options, exact fields eligible to leave the machine, redaction, consent, retention, training policy requirements, prompt and response provenance, budgets, availability, and a no-provider default.

Threat modeling and adversarial fixtures cover source and issue prompt injection, secret exfiltration, untrusted reports, malicious suggestions, provider failure, nondeterminism, and misleading confidence; deferral is an acceptable outcome.

issues.title: Add explicit human approval and remediation review workflow
issues.problemOutcome: Suggestions can bypass ownership and policy accountability if approval, validation, and rejection evidence are not first-class.
acceptanceCriteria: The workflow records suggestion version, reviewer and owner, evidence revision, decision, rationale, validation result, expiry, and final disposition without automatically merging, applying, or weakening policy.
CLI, reports, and optional read-only CI distinguish proposed, approved, rejected, stale, failed-validation, and applied-externally states; least-privilege and fork tests pass.

issues.title: Red-team and evaluate remediation assistance
issues.problemOutcome: Assistance should not graduate on appealing examples while hiding unsafe, irrelevant, or unverifiable recommendations.
acceptanceCriteria: Evaluation measures applicability precision, unsafe suggestion rate, validation success, stale-evidence detection, reviewer acceptance and override, time saved or added, reproducibility, cost, and provider-data exposure by suggestion class.

Red-team cases include injection, secret leakage, destructive commands, policy weakening, broad waivers, dependency confusion, fabricated evidence, compromised providers, and automation bias; a public ADR records graduate, narrow, rule-only, or stop.

issues.title: Create the long-term deprecation and change-control register
issues.problemOutcome: A five-year program needs explicit owners and removal conditions for temporary compatibility paths.
acceptanceCriteria: Every deprecated schema, CLI flag, adapter capability, and policy feature has an owner, review date, replacement, and removal gate.
Release CI reports overdue entries and blocks removal without a migration note and fixture update.

issues.title: Define digest-bound policy bundle federation
issues.problemOutcome: Teams may need shared rules across repositories without requiring a central service or implicit trust.
acceptanceCriteria: A local bundle format records policy source, version, digest, compatibility, owner, and expiry metadata.
Import verifies the digest and compatibility contract offline, and bundles cannot grant network, filesystem, or execution authority.

issues.title: Test policy compatibility, expiry, and revocation migrations
issues.problemOutcome: Federated policy bundles become dangerous when old rules remain active after their assumptions change.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration fixtures cover version upgrades, expiry, explicit revocation, incompatible selectors, and missing owners.
The evaluator produces a digest-only migration report and refuses to enforce an unreviewed incompatible bundle.

issues.title: Rotate and verify assurance signing metadata
issues.problemOutcome: Long-lived assurance bundles need key-rotation and verification semantics that do not imply a hosted trust service.
acceptanceCriteria: The local contract defines signer identity references, rotation, revocation, expiry, and algorithm/version compatibility.
Fixtures cover old keys, missing trust roots, tampered manifests, and explicit verification failure without fallback acceptance.

issues.title: Separate remediation suggestions from canonical findings
issues.problemOutcome: A suggested fix must never mutate architecture evidence or be mistaken for a verified remediation.
acceptanceCriteria: Suggestion records reference findings and proposed edits without changing graph, policy, or history truth.
Reports label suggestions as unverified and reject suggestions whose evidence or baseline digest is stale.

issues.title: Publish a governed architecture-analysis replication corpus
issues.problemOutcome: Independent validation requires stable public inputs and expected evidence, while copied repositories and traces create licensing, privacy, representativeness, and maintenance risks.
acceptanceCriteria: The corpus has provenance, licenses, inclusion and exclusion criteria, versioned tasks, expected outputs, uncertainty annotations, redaction review, maintenance ownership, and a documented process for correction or withdrawal.
It spans supported extraction, identity, diff, policy, ADR, runtime, workspace, workflow, history, and remediation scenarios without implying population-wide representativeness.

issues.title: Run a transparent comparative architecture benchmark
issues.problemOutcome: CARTOGRAPH's value and limitations cannot be understood from internal baselines alone, but tool comparisons are misleading without aligned scope and evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: A preregistered protocol compares selected open or reproducibly accessible tools on overlapping tasks, versions, configurations, hardware, time and resource budgets, supported constructs, evidence quality, unknown behavior, and reviewer tasks.

Raw results and analysis scripts are published; missing features and incomparable outputs are reported explicitly, and no ranking collapses correctness, coverage, usability, security, and performance into one score.

issues.title: Map CARTOGRAPH contracts to portable ecosystem formats
issues.problemOutcome: Architecture evidence remains siloed unless supported findings, provenance, components, and traces can interoperate without losing semantics or overstating equivalence.
acceptanceCriteria: Documented mappings cover selected SARIF, SPDX or CycloneDX, OpenTelemetry, and provenance fields with direction, lossiness, unsupported concepts, identifiers, evidence, and version negotiation.
Round-trip and one-way fixtures quantify preserved, transformed, dropped, and ambiguous information; exports validate against upstream schemas and remain opt-in.

issues.title: Establish an independent replication program
issues.problemOutcome: A self-published corpus and benchmark do not demonstrate that external researchers or maintainers can reproduce the methods and challenge the claims.
acceptanceCriteria: A public protocol defines eligible replications, environment capture, blinded or adversarial cases where practical, issue disclosure, discrepancy handling, citation, contributor credit, and support boundaries.
At least one external replication or structured independent review completes; artifacts, deviations, failures, disagreements, and resulting corrections are published with consent.

issues.title: Publish validated claims, negative results, and limitations
issues.problemOutcome: Five years of engineering and experiments need a durable research record that separates supported conclusions from hypotheses and failed directions.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned report maps each research and product claim to methods, datasets, versions, statistical or qualitative evidence, uncertainty, threats to validity, replications, and contradictory or negative results.

The replication package has archival identifiers where practical, machine-readable metadata, environment instructions, and a correction policy; marketing and README claims are reconciled to the report.

issues.title: Record the interoperability and research gate decision
issues.problemOutcome: Standards and research investment should continue only where mappings, external demand, reproducibility, and maintenance capacity justify them.
acceptanceCriteria: A public ADR evaluates mapping fidelity, upstream engagement, adoption, external replication, claim strength, unresolved discrepancies, security and privacy impact, and ongoing maintenance cost against predeclared gates.
The decision explicitly selects standardization work, maintained adapters only, further research, or closure; rejected directions create no implied compatibility promise.

issues.title: Run a reproducibility study for runtime evidence
issues.problemOutcome: Sampling and environment-dependent traces can produce unstable architecture conclusions.
acceptanceCriteria: Repeated fixture imports under controlled perturbations measure classification stability, missingness, and redaction invariants.
The study publishes method, corpus digest, variance, and explicit non-guarantees without collecting live user traces.

issues.title: Make the runtime feature investment decision
issues.problemOutcome: Runtime reconciliation should not become permanent scope without evidence of reviewer value and acceptable privacy cost.
acceptanceCriteria: A public ADR weighs reproducibility, privacy/security findings, adoption feedback, maintenance cost, and static-only usefulness.
The decision authorizes bounded follow-up issues or explicitly defers/sunsets runtime work without leaving hidden collection paths.

issues.title: Publish the ownership and waiver governance gate
issues.problemOutcome: Governance metadata should not become an unbounded collaboration product without evidence of local value.
acceptanceCriteria: A public gate report audits source precedence, signed/expiry behavior, drift detection, privacy, and reviewer usefulness.
The decision authorizes bounded maintenance/integration work or explicitly defers the surface without leaving implicit authority paths.

issues.title: Publish the assurance-surface decision gate
issues.problemOutcome: Assurance packaging can become a compliance product without sufficient evidence of architecture-review value.
acceptanceCriteria: A gate report weighs independent replay, provenance integrity, redaction, adoption, maintainer cost, and claim limitations.
The project records a bounded continuation, maintenance-only mode, or explicit defer/sunset decision with linked tasks.

issues.title: Publish the architecture-history investment gate
issues.problemOutcome: Trend analysis should not become an analytics platform without evidence of reliable architecture decisions.
acceptanceCriteria: A gate report audits provenance, missingness, privacy, storage, performance, reviewer usefulness, and maintenance burden.
The project authorizes bounded follow-up, maintenance-only mode, or explicit defer/sunset with a public rationale.

issues.title: Publish the remediation-assistance decision gate
issues.problemOutcome: Automated suggestions are not justified unless they improve review outcomes without weakening evidence or control.
acceptanceCriteria: A study measures suggestion precision, accepted/rejected patches, reviewer effort, security failures, rollback success, and privacy cost.
A public ADR authorizes bounded continuation, local-only maintenance, or explicit defer/sunset without enabling unreviewed mutation.

issues.title: Define and cut the five-year LTS release line
issues.problemOutcome: Long-term users need a bounded support promise that separates stable contracts from experiments and does not exceed maintainer capacity.
acceptanceCriteria: The LTS policy names supported runtime, platforms, schemas, snapshots, policies, adapters, workspace and history formats, Action versions, security fixes, deprecation windows, experimental exclusions, release cadence, and end-of-support date.

A reproducible signed release passes the full compatibility matrix, package and Action smoke tests, migration checks, assurance replay, security gates, and documented rollback before the line is announced.

issues.title: Rehearse end-to-end migration, recovery, and downgrade
issues.problemOutcome: An LTS promise is weak unless representative users can move from prior formats and recover safely from failed or incompatible upgrades.
acceptanceCriteria: A clean environment migrates every supported snapshot, policy, adapter, workspace, finding-lifecycle, assurance, and history version through documented steps while preserving originals and producing equivalence reports.

Tabletop and automated scenarios cover interruption, corruption, insufficient disk, revoked signatures, adapter removal, partial workspace, rollback, backup restore, and unsupported downgrade with measured recovery time.

issues.title: Complete the LTS security and reproducibility audit
issues.problemOutcome: Long support windows amplify dependency, build, key, provenance, parser, workflow, and incident-response risks.
acceptanceCriteria: The audit covers threat models, dependency and action pinning, build provenance, artifact verification, signing and rotation, supported parsers and adapters, fuzz regressions, CI permissions, release process, disclosure, patch SLAs, and reproducible rebuilds.

Critical and high findings are resolved or explicitly block release; medium findings have owners and dates, an independent review path is recorded, and the public summary distinguishes completed tests from unperformed work.

issues.title: Establish maintainer succession and sustainable governance
issues.problemOutcome: An LTS release and public evidence corpus cannot depend on one person's indefinite availability or unfunded operational work.
acceptanceCriteria: The governance plan defines maintainer roles, decision rights, security and release backups, access recovery, succession, conflict handling, funding disclosure, sponsor boundaries, archival triggers, and transfer or sunset procedures.

At least two authorized maintainers or documented fallback custodians complete access, release, vulnerability-triage, roadmap, and recovery drills; unresolved capacity gaps constrain the support promise.

issues.title: Publish the five-year technical, market, and research retrospective
issues.problemOutcome: The next strategy should be based on shipped outcomes, user value, costs, external evidence, and failed bets rather than backlog completion or vanity metrics.
acceptanceCriteria: The retrospective compares original and revised goals with releases, compatibility, correctness, performance, security, incidents, adoption and retention, contributor health, support load, cost, revenue or funding where applicable, citations, replications, and negative results.

It distinguishes causal evidence from correlation and anecdotes, names discontinued and deferred work, audits current claims, includes stakeholder dissent, and publishes reusable lessons and open questions.

issues.title: Record the next-horizon continue, scale, transfer, or sunset decision
issues.problemOutcome: A mature project needs an explicit terminal decision instead of automatically rolling unfinished ambition into another roadmap.
acceptanceCriteria: A public ADR evaluates user value, strategic differentiation, research contribution, market evidence, security posture, maintenance and opportunity cost, funding, governance capacity, ecosystem fit, and credible alternatives using predeclared thresholds.

The decision selects and funds a bounded next program, maintains LTS only, transfers stewardship, or executes a safe sunset; each branch names owners, dates, user migration, security obligations, data and artifact disposition, and success or completion evidence.
